limits: The real test used Nov10 W2L, confirmed by user; latest policy has no corresponding real test in local evidence.
Latest model replay is counterfactual and held to the old measured history; it does not generate a new real trajectory.
One-row lag is a reconstruction assumption, not a measured hardware latency.
The original W2L replay retains approx5.09/4.59deg hip target RMSE; inferred inputs are not independently logged network tensors.
Local sensitivities do not determine robot stability or isolate the effect of two simultaneous reward changes.

method.derivative: Central differences for each physical hip input, each of10 history lags; output physical hip target radians. Other observations and recorded previous actions remain fixed.
method.frequency: Frozen local kernels sum_l J_l exp(-i2pi*f*l*0.02); previous-action branch extra20ms delay stored separately. This is policy response, not measured closed-loop or motor transfer function.
method.inputs: Reuse hash-validated real-observation histories from prior analysis. Both W2L policies receive exactly identical 590-dimensional inputs. Wheel receives re-encoded histories of the same physical states and previous physical targets; task-specific commands differ.
method.scalar: Largest singular value of2x2 bilateral physical Jacobian, median and95th percentile over45 operating points. Rows outputR/L, columns inputR/L.
method.target_spectrum: Feed recorded state and recorded previous targets; no autoregressive rollout. Detrend each45-point output with least-squares line; Hann-window rFFT; sum unnormalized power at7–13Hz. Same window and units; no claim of closed-loop stability.
